```{r load-data}
# load your data 
sample_submission <- read_csv("data/sample_submission.csv")
test <- read_csv("data/test.csv")
train <- read_csv("data/train.csv")
```

```{r cleaning}
# Cleaning sample_submission
glimpse(sample_submission)
sum(is.na(sample_submission))
#sample_submission is clean by default
```

```{r cleaning}
# Cleaning train
clean_names(train)
train <- train %>%
  mutate(MSSubClass_fctr = as.factor(MSSubClass),
         OverallQual_fctr = as.factor(OverallQual),
         OverallCond_fctr = as.factor(OverallCond),
         ExterQual_fctr = as.factor(ExterQual),
         ExterCond_fctr = as.factor(ExterCond),
         BsmtQual_fctr = as.factor(BsmtQual),
         BsmtCond_fctr = as.factor(BsmtCond),
         BsmtExposure_fctr = as.factor(BsmtExposure),
         BsmtFinType1_fctr = as.factor(BsmtFinType1),
         BsmtFinType2_fctr = as.factor(BsmtFinType2),
         HeatingQC_fctr = as.factor(HeatingQC),
         KitchenQual_fctr = as.factor(KitchenQual),
         Functional_fctr = as.factor(Functional),
         FireplaceQu_fctr = as.factor(FireplaceQu),
         GarageQual_fctr = as.factor(GarageQual),
         GarageFinish_fctr = as.factor(GarageFinish),
         GarageCond_fctr = as.factor(GarageCond),
         PoolQC_fctr = as.factor(PoolQC),
         Fence_fctr = as.factor(Fence))
train %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~n_distinct(.x))) %>%
  select(where(~.x == 0))
  
# demonstrates that there are no columns with no arguments, hence this data frame must have no useless columns.
```

```{r}

```

```{r}
test_price <- test %>%
  full_join(sample_submission, by = 'Id')
test_price %>%
  summarise(avg_price = mean(SalePrice, na.rm = TRUE),
            med_price = median(SalePrice, na.rm = TRUE),
            q25_price = quantile(SalePrice, probs = 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
            q75_price = quantile(SalePrice, probs = 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_price = sd(SalePrice, na.rm = TRUE),
            min_price = min(SalePrice, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_price = max(SalePrice, na.rm = TRUE))
test_price %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = `SalePrice`)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20)
```

# We have worked out that the mean price and median price is the same to 3 significance figure accuracy, this suggests that the distribution of sales price for housing could be approximated to a normal distribution and almost symmetrical, implying that there are no outliers in our data.
